clue.text: Call for artist to produce exciting work

blocks.note: to page someone is to call them over a public address system
J. M. W. Turner, the English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A summons for a painter to come and create a thrilling piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A page-turner is a book so gripping that readers keep flipping on to find out what happens next.

clue.text: In formal agreement, not professional to display insincerity

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the other, enclosed by the agreement

blocks.note: a pact is a treaty or formal agreement
lay means amateur, not a member of a profession

explanation.surface: An amateur shows false feelings while signing a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: To play-act is to pretend or put on a show of feeling one does not have.

clue.text: Semiconductor material in mass imported by plant

indicators.note: something imported is brought inside, so it sits within the other word

blocks.note: the geranium is a common flowering garden plant
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A garden flower takes in a quantity of a substance used for chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Germanium is a chemical element whose semiconducting property made it vital to early transistors.

clue.text: The very person recorded in Screwtape Letters

blocks.note: first meaning: the exclamation when the person just mentioned turns up
second meaning, read literally: C. S. Lewis's book is letters written by a senior demon, so it is a fiend's own words set down

explanation.surface: Someone appears who features in a famous book of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is said when the person just mentioned turns up; The Screwtape Letters is C. S. Lewis's book of advice from one demon to another.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom greets someone who arrives just as they were mentioned, and Lewis's book is literally speech from a devil.

clue.text: More prepared to accept decline in breed

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: to rear animals is to breed them
to die away is to fade or decline

explanation.surface: Someone more willing to tolerate falling numbers in a pedigree line.
explanation.definitionFit: Readier is the comparative of ready, meaning better prepared or more willing.

clue.text: Apostle converting a couple of characters as part of his work

indicators.note: converting two characters means two letters of the word are swapped for others

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disciple changing a few words in what he wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: The A becomes E and the O becomes I; the whole clue also describes the answer, since apostles such as Paul wrote the epistles.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a letter, and the New Testament epistles are letters written by apostles.

clue.text: Poet's old verse I had abridged

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
V is the abbreviation for verse
'I had' shortens to I'd, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A poet's ancient lines, which I once possessed in a shortened edition.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Poet', with the 's read as 'is' joining it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman writer of the Metamorphoses and the Art of Love.

clue.text: Spitefulness of five thousand and one held up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top
held means kept inside the letters around it

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral five
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Anger at a large number of people being delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom figuratively means bitter malice, like poison in words or manner.

clue.text: Affect the mind with a gender change

indicators.note: a change of order lets the letters come out differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Changing sex is said to disturb a person's psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to make someone insane, disturbing their mental balance.

clue.text: Agreed in one minute. Ketch - hang them all!

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for minute
all right is said to show agreement
Jack Ketch was a notorious seventeenth-century English hangman

explanation.surface: A hangman swiftly consents to execute everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch's name became English slang for any executioner, which ties to 'hang'; the phrase is an exclamation of smug selfishness.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase expresses complacent indifference to others once one's own comfort is secured, like damning the rest.

clue.text: Line written on distinctive atmosphere of hearing

indicators.note: in an across entry, something written on another comes straight after it in the row

blocks.note: an aura is the special feeling surrounding a person or place
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A sentence inscribed about the special mood of a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural is the adjective relating to the ear and the sense through which sound is perceived.

clue.text: Ancient region, a kingdom in love with monarch

blocks.note: taken as written
Siam is the old name of the kingdom of Thailand
taken as written
love is a score of nil in tennis, written as O
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: An old territory where a realm is besotted with its sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor is the classical name for Anatolia, the peninsula making up most of modern Turkey.

clue.text: Gray, for example, or Burton, sadly?

blocks.note: first meaning: Henry Gray, author of the textbook Gray's Anatomy
second meaning: Robert Burton, who wrote The Anatomy of Melancholy, dissecting sadness

explanation.surface: Naming famous Grays and Burtons, the latter looking glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' points at Burton's book title, The Anatomy of Melancholy; Gray's Anatomy is the classic medical textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men produced works titled as anatomies, the medical one literally about dissecting the body's structure.

clue.text: Paris paper largely supplies useless article

indicators.note: largely means most but not all of the name is used, so its tail end is cut

blocks.note: Le Monde is the leading Paris daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A French newspaper mostly fills its pages with worthless items.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of the paper's name are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is slang for a dud product, especially a faulty car that never works properly.

clue.text: Criminal type creating quite a storm

blocks.note: first meaning: a swindler or cheat
second meaning: a tornado or whirlwind

explanation.surface: A villain stirring up a great fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is both a dishonest person who cheats others and an informal American name for a tornado.

clue.text: Travelling in France, force to fly in various directions

blocks.note: en is French for in
to rout an army is to put it to disorderly flight
E for east, one compass point taken to stand for the many

explanation.surface: On a trip through France, an army is made to scatter and flee.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: rout supplies most of the letters, and the final E must come from the compass-point direction.
explanation.definitionFit: En route means on the way, so someone travelling toward a destination is en route.

clue.text: One sort of Christian group raised money in Lagos

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is turned upward, read bottom to top

blocks.note: a unit is a group forming part of a larger body
the naira is the currency of Nigeria, where Lagos is

explanation.surface: A church congregation collects funds in Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Unitarians are Christians who reject the Trinity and hold that God is a single being.

clue.text: In part of Bible, really boring bits?

blocks.note: first meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament
second meaning: things that deaden feeling, from numb, with the dull lists of the book in mind

explanation.surface: A reader complaining about the tedious passages of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The book of the Old Testament is famously full of census lists, hence 'boring'; the second reading takes the word as 'things that numb'.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers is the biblical book named for its counts of the Israelites, and numbers are also things that numb.

clue.text: Form of justice people upset resist heartily

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so in a down entry the word is read upward
heartily means only the heart, the central letters, are taken

blocks.note: men stands for people
the four central letters of the word

explanation.surface: Citizens rise up and fight a kind of judicial system with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of retribution, and the word means just punishment that catches up with wrongdoers.

clue.text: I wish a different line to be taken in African speech

indicators.note: different means arranged otherwise, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line, here added to the mix

explanation.surface: A speaker hopes for another approach in an address to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu language spoken widely across East Africa as a lingua franca.

clue.text: Pushy parents ensure their infants make progress in them

definitions.text: Pushy parents ensure their infants make progress in them

blocks.clueFragment: Pushy parents ensure their infants make progress
blocks.note: surface reading: ambitious parents driving children to get ahead

blocks.clueFragment: Pushy parents ensure their infants make progress in them
blocks.note: setter's reading: parents literally push the little ones along in wheeled chairs

explanation.surface: Ambitious mothers and fathers making sure their babies advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Buggies are lightweight folding pushchairs in which small children are wheeled about.

clue.text: Made present of book - draft taking time to complete

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
a rough is a first draft or sketch
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A book given as a gift, its first version taking ages to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made present' looks like gave a gift, but means caused to be present.
explanation.definitionFit: To have brought someone or something is to have caused them to be present in a place.

clue.text: Flats, for example, visible from house

blocks.note: first meaning: in a theatre, flats are painted canvas panels on the stage
second meaning: the house is the theatre audience, and this is the stage picture they see

explanation.surface: Looking out of a home window at blocks of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre, flats are wooden frames of painted canvas and the house is the auditorium, so this is what the audience sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage scenery is made up of painted backdrops and flats that the audience watches from the seats.

clue.text: Fly back, for example, in poor visibility

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
dim means poorly lit or hard to see

explanation.surface: An insect returning, say, through fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny two-winged insect, a gnat-like fly that swarms near water.

clue.text: Be killed around end of war - grand lamentation

indicators.note: around means wrapping round the letters that follow
end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: to die is to be killed
the final letter of the word
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Falling at the close of a war, mourned with a great lament.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song sung at a funeral, a musical lament for the dead.

clue.text: Where one applies razor in reverse order

blocks.note: first meaning, split as two words: around the face
second meaning: a military command to turn round, or a complete change of policy

explanation.surface: Shaving instructions given backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a parade-ground command to turn to the rear, and so any total reversal of direction.

clue.text: Working hard, succeeded with education

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
training is instruction or schooling

explanation.surface: Someone toils and gets on in life through schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining means making a great effort, exerting oneself to the limit.

clue.text: From spite, dropped married woman

indicators.note: dropped says a letter is let fall from the word before it

blocks.note: malice is a desire to harm, spite
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: Out of spite, a husband abandoned his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a girl's name, so it stands for any woman in crossword fashion.

clue.text: Swing round uncontrollably and get killed

definitions.note: slew is the past tense of slay, so it means killed rather than get killed

blocks.note: first meaning: a skidding vehicle ... across the road
second meaning: past tense of slay

explanation.surface: A car spins out of control and its driver dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To slew is to swerve or skid sideways, and slew is also the past form of slay, meaning murdered.

clue.text: By accident, it's my ankle that's damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone explains an injured ankle came from a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistakenly means in error, unintentionally, which is what happens when something occurs by accident.
